name: Erdene Zuu Monastery (Ancient Karakorum)
builtBy: Abtai Sain Khan (Built on ruins of Karakorum)
description: Oldest surviving Buddhist monastery in Mongolia, built within the perimeter walls of Karakorum, the 13th-century imperial capital of Genghis Khan.
history: Karakorum was founded by Genghis Khan in 1220 as the political hub from which the Mongol Empire commanded Eurasia.
construction: Enclosed by a massive 400x400 meter stone wall studded with 108 sacred Buddhist stupas.
architecture: Combines Chinese, Tibetan, and traditional Mongol nomadic architectural elements with preserved stone turtles.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape.
currentStatus: Active museum and monastery in Ovorkhangai Province, Mongolia.
